scenarios.name: Hero Section Implementation
scenarios.description: Validates the hero section displays project name, tagline, animated logo, and call-to-action buttons correctly

steps.description: Build the hero section with proper semantic HTML including header, h1 for project name, tagline paragraph, and CTA buttons
steps.context: REQ-1: Hero Section - Must display MirDB name, tagline, and CTAs

steps.description: Apply CSS for full viewport height, dark theme background, centered content, and responsive typography
steps.context: Visual Design: Dark theme with Rust orange #DEA584 accent colors

steps.description: Include the animated GIF logo with proper alt text and loading optimization
steps.context: Assets: logo.gif from assets directory

steps.description: Create primary (GitHub) and secondary (Get Started) buttons with hover states
steps.context: Primary CTA links to GitHub, secondary to documentation

test_cases.input: Load landing page and inspect hero section
test_cases.expected: Hero section is visible with full viewport height, contains 'MirDB' as h1, tagline 'A Persistent Key-Value Store with Memcached Protocol', animated logo, and two CTA buttons
Opens GitHub repository link (https://github.com/yetone/mirdb) in new tab with rel='noopener noreferrer'
Smooth scrolls to Usage/Documentation section or links to quick start guide
Logo has descriptive alt text, lazy loading disabled (above fold), and displays animated GIF
Hero section adapts responsively: logo scales down, typography adjusts, buttons stack vertically

scenarios.name: Technical Architecture Section
scenarios.description: Validates architecture diagram, component breakdown, and data flow visualization

steps.context: REQ-4: Technical Architecture - system diagram and component breakdown

steps.description: Include SVG or image diagram showing memtable, SSTables, compaction, and network layer

steps.description: Create expandable or inline explanations for each architecture component
steps.context: Help contributors identify areas for contribution

steps.description: Show write path (client -> memtable -> SSTable) and read path with visual elements
steps.context: Technical users need to understand data flow

test_cases.expected: Section displays heading, architecture diagram, and component breakdown
Diagram shows: Network Layer (Tokio), Memtable (Skip List), Immutable Memtable, SSTables (L0-L6), Compaction Engine
Diagram has descriptive alt text or aria-label explaining the architecture visually depicted
Explains in-memory skip list structure, 4MB default size, write buffering purpose
Explains sorted string tables, 100MB max size, block-based structure, multi-level organization
Explains minor compaction (memtable to SSTable) and major compaction (level merging)
Diagram scales or scrolls horizontally, component cards stack vertically
